title: BPR&D Reference: First Responder Handbook - Computer System Acquisition
summary: Official National Standard from First Responder Handbook - Computer System Acquisition. Section: System Acquisition: Windows Live BitLocker Disabling.
decisionReason: Official standard issued by BPR&D.
implementationOutcome: Nationally notified guideline for law enforcement officers.
sourceDocument: First Responder Handbook - Computer System Acquisition
text: When acquiring a Windows workstation where BitLocker encryption is enabled by default, the first responder can check and disable encryption directly from an elevated administrative command prompt without needing a recovery key. Run `manage-bde -off <DriveLetter>:` across all partitions (e.g., `manage-bde -off C:`, `manage-bde -off D:`, `manage-bde -off E:`). Verify the ongoing status using `manage-bde -status`. Ensure 'Conversion Status' shows 'Fully Decrypted', 'Percentage Encrypted' reaches 0.0%, and 'Protection Status' is 'Protection Off'. After complete decryption, connect a sterile target external drive via USB 3.0, launch AccessData FTK Imager, select 'Physical Drive' as the source evidence type, choose E01 (Expert Witness format), enter case number and evidence number, and compute MD5 and SHA-1 verification hashes to ensure evidence integrity.

title: BPR&D Reference: First Responder Handbook - Computer System Acquisition
summary: Official National Standard from First Responder Handbook - Computer System Acquisition. Section: System Acquisition: Linux Live System Acquisition.
decisionReason: Official standard issued by BPR&D.
implementationOutcome: Nationally notified guideline for law enforcement officers.
sourceDocument: First Responder Handbook - Computer System Acquisition
text: For live acquisition of a Linux system, first isolate the machine from network connections. Open terminal and run `sudo fdisk -l` to identify the source block device (e.g., `/dev/sda`) and the destination storage (e.g., `/dev/sdb`). Use `dcfldd` instead of traditional `dd` due to enhanced forensic hashing capabilities. Execute: `dcfldd if=/dev/sda of=/media/ext_drive/sda_image.img hash=md5,sha256 md5log=md5.txt sha256log=sha256.txt bs=4k conv=noerror,sync split=2G splitformat=img status=on`. In this command, `bs=4k` sets the block size, `conv=noerror,sync` prevents termination on read errors while zero-filling corrupted blocks, and `split=2G` breaks the image into 2 GB chunks. Volatile memory should be captured beforehand using AVML (Acquire Volatile Memory for Linux). Document the entire execution chain in the Chain of Custody form.

title: BPR&D Reference: Proceedings of National Level Webinar on Prevention and Investigation of Phishing Crimes
summary: Official National Standard from Proceedings of National Level Webinar on Prevention and Investigation of Phishing Crimes. Section: Hard AI Problems Based Novel Adaptive Approach Against Phishing.
decisionReason: Official standard issued by BPR&D.
implementationOutcome: Nationally notified guideline for law enforcement officers.
sourceDocument: Proceedings of National Level Webinar on Prevention and Investigation of Phishing Crimes
text: Dr. Puneet Goyal (IIT Ropar) introduced the Multimedia Content Set Particular to User (MCSPU) model as a Hard AI-based proactive enterprise defense against Phishing and Man-in-the-Browser (MitB) attacks. Traditional SSL certificates and padlock icons merely secure transmission channels but do not validate website authenticity. Under the MCSPU model, during banking transactions or logins, the bank presents an image containing user-specified embedded text and parameters selected from a personal image set registered beforehand. Attackers cannot dynamically alter embedded text in natural scene images without introducing detectable artifacts within transaction timeout windows. The adaptive framework requires users to identify their personalized image among alternatives, defeating automated credential harvesting bots and phishing proxies.

title: BPR&D Reference: Proceedings of National Level Webinar on Prevention and Investigation of Phishing Crimes
summary: Official National Standard from Proceedings of National Level Webinar on Prevention and Investigation of Phishing Crimes. Section: Critical Information Infrastructure Threats & The Triton Malware Vector.
decisionReason: Official standard issued by BPR&D.
implementationOutcome: Nationally notified guideline for law enforcement officers.
sourceDocument: Proceedings of National Level Webinar on Prevention and Investigation of Phishing Crimes
text: In Session 3, Sh. Sanjeev Relia addressed the vulnerabilities of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) in India, governed under Section 70A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 by NCIIPC (a unit of NTRO under the PMO). Critical sectors include Power & Energy, Telecom, Transport, BFSI, Government, and Strategic Enterprises. Primary threats are Espionage, Subversion, and Sabotage. A prime case study was the 2017 Triton/Trisis malware attack against a Saudi petrochemical plant, which targeted Triconex Safety Instrumented System (SIS) controllers manufactured by Schneider Electric. Spear-phishing served as the initial intrusion vector into the corporate IT network, after which attackers pivoted into the Industrial Control System (ICS/DCS) network, posing direct hazards of toxic gas releases and explosions. Mitigation requires network air-gapping, R&D-embedded cybersecurity, and adherence to CEA Cyber Security Regulations.

title: BPR&D Reference: Latest WhatsApp Scams
summary: Official National Standard from Latest WhatsApp Scams. Section: WhatsApp Account Hijacking via MMI Call Forwarding Codes.
decisionReason: Official standard issued by BPR&D / I4C.
implementationOutcome: Nationally notified guideline for law enforcement officers.
text: WhatsApp account hijacking exploits telecom Unstructured Supplementary Service Data (USSD) / Man-Machine Interface (MMI) call-forwarding codes. Fraudsters call the target victim and employ social engineering or pretexting to induce them to dial an MMI string such as '*67*<10-digit-phone-number>#' or '*405*<10-digit-phone-number>#'. Once dialed, the victim's carrier automatically enables unconditional or busy call forwarding to the fraudster's number. Simultaneously, the fraudster attempts to register WhatsApp using the victim's phone number on their device and opts to receive the one-time verification passcode (OTP) via voice call. Because the victim's line is engaged, the automated verification call is routed directly to the fraudster's phone, granting complete unauthorized access to the victim's account. This enables secondary scams including extortion, impersonating executives, and soliciting urgent payments.

title: BPR&D Reference: Compendium of Security Equipment Used in Prisons
summary: Official National Standard from Compendium of Security Equipment Used in Prisons. Section: Perimeter Pulse Fence Technical Specifications.
decisionReason: Official standard issued by BPR&D.
implementationOutcome: Nationally notified guideline for law enforcement officers.
sourceDocument: Compendium of Security Equipment Used in Prisons
text: Technical standards for prison Perimeter Pulse Fences mandate full compliance with IEC 60335-2-76 and IS 302-2-76. The energizer delivered energy must not exceed 5 Joules into a 500 Ohm load, with regulated pulse intervals of not less than 1.1 seconds. Operating in Live-Earth configuration across 100-150 meter zones, high-voltage operation delivers 6 kV to 8 kV, with a low-voltage safe mode of 0.4 kV to 1.0 kV. Upon sustained intrusion detection, the controller transitions to HV Plus mode, delivering up to 10 kV for 20 minutes. Intelligent Field Controllers must buffer up to 80,000 offline events, feature on-board 10/100 Ethernet with IPv4/IPv6 support, and use 128-bit AES encrypted RS-485 serial communication to peripheral fence units. The mechanical structure requires 50 NB MS hot-dip galvanized end posts (min. 60-micron zinc coating) with internal unscalable anti-climb geometry.
